To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thermoelectric cooling is not feasible in a thin substrate and that only a small positive cooling temperature is measured between the anode and cathode contacts.

1) the substrate has a large impact on the thermal resistance and the cooling capacity of thermoelectric devices; 2) for materials with a small ZT value the substrate will have a larger influence on the cooling power than the thermoelectric material itself; and 3) the experimental measurement of the small positive temperature difference between the anode and the cathode contacts can be misread as cooling when in reality it is heating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of micro-coolers for integrated circuits.
understanding the fundamental physics of micro-coolers, and the development of micro-coolermaterials, devices and systems.
the thermal management of integrated electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the substrate will have a significant impact on the cooling capacity and it is necessary to measure the cooling power of the thermoelectrics in the presence of a substrate.

the cooling capacity of a thermoelectric cooler is not simply a function of the thermoelectrical properties of the thermoelements, but rather is dependent on the thermoelectro-thermal properties of the entire thermoelectric cooler.
the thermoelectric effect cannot be used to cool a substrate, such as a silicon wafer, that is much thicker than the thermal penetration depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for thermoelectric cool power density, the substrate has to be thinned to obtain the cooling and the substrate thermal conductivity has to be minimized to maximize the cooling.

thermoelectric coolings can provide a significant cooling capacity in integrated circuits but the supporting substrate has to be thin and the thermoelectric cooling device has to be designed to minimize the heat conduction from the substrate.
for thermoelectric cooling to work, it is important to consider the substrate material and the thermal boundary conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal resistance between the substrate and the thermoelectric device is a critical parameter in determining the cooling capacity.
the cooling temperature difference between the anode and the cathode contacts of a micro-cooler should be measured and not the small positive temperature difference between the Th and Tc contacts.
the substrate has a large impact on the cooling capacity and that ΔT measurements alone are not sufficient to determine the direction of heat flux.
